newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's real falls 0.23 pct on low dlr liquidity.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's real falls 0.23 pct on low dlr liquidity.

text.p: Brazil's real fell 0.23 percent to close at 1.0615 reais per dollar in the commercial foreign exchange market, after the central bank sold dollars at an auction to increase liquidity in the market, dealers said.

The central bank sold dollars at 1.0615 reais per greenback to help some banks square off their positions at the end of the day and maintain the dollar within the trading level of 1.0565 and 1.0615 reais per dollars, they added.
Traders noted that scarcity of dollars in the market made the real drop 0.24 percent during the session to 1.0616 per dollar, which is 0.01 percent above the mini-band.
In the interbank foreign exchange floating rate market, the real rose a slight 0.01 percent to end at 1.0619 reais per dollar.
In the illegal parallel market, the real fell 0.92 percent to end at 1.100 reais per greenback.
